LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING/BRAILLE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting/braille writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting/braille writing, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write words neatly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting/braille writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn; the learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they practice forming ascenders and descenders/ braille letters b, d, f,

h, q, y, j, neatly correctly as an aspect of good handwriting/braille writing.

• Communication and collaboration; the learner’s writing skills are improved as they copy long words with the target letter-sound combinations (fl- and -ey), clearly and correctly.

Values:
Responsibility; the learner’s ability to care for one's own and other’s property is enhanced as they take care of digital devices when watching/listening

to videos.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Learner Support Programmes; (Peer education and mentorship) The learner interpersonal relationships are enhanced as they assist others improve

their handwriting/braille writing.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Good handwriting/braille writing is essential in all learning areas.
